newsitem.title: USA: Saudi pleads not guilty in U.S. court to bomb plot.
newsitem.headline: Saudi pleads not guilty in U.S. court to bomb plot.

text.p: A Saudi dissident allegedly linked to the 1996 bombing in Saudi Arabia that killed 19 U.S. servicemen pleaded not guilty on Wednesday to unrelated criminal charges of plotting an earlier unsuccessful attack.

Hani al-Sayegh, who was deported from Canada last month, repudiated an earlier agreement in which he would have pleaded guilty to the single conspiracy charge of plotting to kill Americans in Saudi Arabia in return for his cooperation with the U.S. investigation into the Khobar Towers bombing.

The judge set a jury trial for Nov. 3 on the charge of conspiring to commit murder and "international terrorism," starting in January 1994 and lasting until December 1995. He ordered Sayegh, 28, to remain in jail without bond.

After the court hearing, defence attorney Francis Carter told reporters he had attempted to negotiate a new plea deal with U.S. prosecutors but talks had broken off on Monday and he did not expect them to resume.

Carter maintained he had no information that Sayegh "knows about" the truck bombing that killed 19 U.S. airmen and injured 500 at the Khobar Towers U.S. military housing complex on an airbase near Dhahran on Saudi Arabia's east coast. Canadian court documents have identified Sayegh as the driver of a car that gave the truck a go-ahead signal to carry out the bombing.

Carter said he had no idea whether prosecutors would bring charges against Sayegh in the Khobar Towers bombing, but said the U.S. government had "no documentary evidence" linking Sayegh to the attack or any other criminal acts.
